title: retry.sh rerun ordering: Protect is submitted last, only after every other rerun request succeeds
answers: Why did Protect fail immediately and use up an attempt when another rerun failed?
Why is the protect.yml workflow rerun delayed until after the other reruns?
Where is the Protect-last rerun ordering in the retry script?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/retry.sh (the `rerun` function and the while-read loop over eligible rows) submits `gh run rerun --failed` for each eligible failed workflow; the protect.yml run is identified from its workflow resourcePath and held back.
Rule: Submit non-Protect reruns in parallel as background jobs, wait for all of them, then submit the Protect rerun only if every preceding rerun request succeeded. Keep a nonzero exit status when any request failed so the next scheduled run retries.
Symptom: When one non-Protect rerun request failed, Protect was still submitted and failed right away (protect.js stopped it while the other workflow stayed failed), spending a Protect attempt and possibly exhausting the commit-wide retry budget.
Constraints: The wait covers the rerun requests, not the reruns' own completion. Verified with mocked parallel requests on both success and failure paths; no real reruns were submitted during validation.
applies: Scope: rerun dispatch order in .github/workflows/retry.sh; not protect.js or protect.yml logic itself.
says: The protection check fails immediately and consumes a retry attempt when another rerun request fails.
Branch protection retries are exhausting our retry budget because other workflow reruns failed.
Wait until all other retry requests succeed before dispatching the final branch protection rerun.
Do not launch the protection workflow rerun if any preceding rerun submission encounters an error.
search: In .github/workflows/retry.sh, non-Protect failed workflow reruns are dispatched in parallel as background jobs using gh run rerun --failed, and protect.yml is submitted last only if every preceding rerun request succeeded. If any rerun request fails, the script maintains a nonzero exit status so the next scheduled run can retry without wasting a Protect attempt. The waiting logic applies to dispatching rerun requests rather than waiting for workflow completion, and does not alter protect.js or protect.yml logic.
